title: Szilassi polyhedra: every seven-hexagon torus without overarching faces has exactly one convex face, and no symmetric 12-face Szilassi polyhedron exists (computer-assisted proofs with DRAT certificates)
description:
In plain words. Szilassi's polyhedron is a ring-shaped solid made of seven flat hexagons, each sharing an edge with all the others. In 2009 Grünbaum and Szilassi conjectured that every ring-shaped polyhedron built only from hexagons has at least six dented (non-convex) faces. We settle the seven-hexagon case for rings in which every two hexagons share an edge: every such polyhedron has exactly one un-dented face, never two and never none. Szilassi's polyhedron (1977) and the tetrahedron are the only two polyhedra known in which every face shares an edge with every other face. The next possible solid of this kind would have 12 faces; whether it exists has been open since the 1970s. We proved it cannot have any symmetry other than doing nothing. Whether a lopsided one exists is still open.

The idea in one picture. proving that a sudoku has no solution. You could try every filling, but a written chain of deductions ending in a contradiction is a proof anyone can re-check line by line. Here the squares are yes/no facts about the shape, a SAT solver does the deducing, and it writes its chain to a proof file that a separate small program re-checks. Where the picture breaks. a sudoku's rules are exact, while here the rules are necessary conditions written by us as code, so the proof is only as good as that translation; each translation was tested against exact geometry, and for Part A written twice, independently.

For specialists. Part A (new in v1.1). Theorem. Every acoptic polyhedral torus with exactly seven hexagonal faces and no overarching faces (definitions of Grünbaum and Szilassi 2009) has exactly one convex face. Hence their Conjecture 5.7 holds, with equality, for seven-face hexangulations without overarching faces; seven-face hexangulations with overarching faces are not covered. Proof: such a polyhedron realises Szilassi's map; two independently written rank-4 oriented-matroid SAT encodings of embedded realisations, with convex-face constraints, are unsatisfiable for 'at least two convex faces' and for 'no convex face'; every UNSAT answer has a DRAT proof verified by drat-trim. Szilassi's published coordinates are checked in exact arithmetic (embedded, exactly one convex face). Folder convex7/ reproduces everything with one command.

Part B (v1.0). No polyhedron with 12 faces in which every two faces share an edge has a non-trivial symmetry (36 SAT instances, all UNSAT with verified DRAT proofs; the asymmetric case remains open).

Links. Repository, with a plain-language guide: github.com/Hashirama1337s/szilassi-12. All projects: the Moki & Julio lab map.

Prepared with AI assistance; what was checked, and by what, is stated above.
